scope: Audio cue and track source-preserving proposals
Registered resource selection and host race guards
Shared PCM WAV validation and Godot adapter fingerprint
Verified byte snapshot, Web Audio lifecycle and pause/resume/seek
Read-only scene audio identity directory and authenticated HTTP integration
Behavior parameter track picker and source ownership
New evidence inventory and common credential patterns

securityInventory.note: New files are source/tests and seven evidence directories; logs/screenshots are intentional preserved evidence, not disposable build output. Pattern scan is a targeted review, not a proof that every possible secret is absent.

freshTests.mode: Direct node execution of each node:test file; two processes maximum
freshTests.runnerNote: An initial node --test call passed all six files but only reported file-level totals in this environment. Direct execution then verified 123 individual test cases; file summaries are kept separately.

boundaries.detail: Audition verifies a copied byte snapshot and rechecks source/catalog before decoding. Pause/resume/seek reuse this verified buffer; they do not certify later on-disk changes.
One transient WAV player; no cue timeline or Godot/Bevy runtime playback transport.
Directory checks saved Scene2D v2/v3 registration, explicit audio relation and audio document semantics. It is not a WAV availability or full engine build check.
Explicitly inserted track IDs remain ordinary string parameters; no inferred track_id semantics or persistent reference protection.

Existing evidence does not establish installed Tauri, physical audio output or Android device behavior. Release notes must keep these limitations distinct from source/browser/prepared-copy verification.

conclusion: No reproducible release-blocking problem found in the audited increment. Historical evidence and author data should remain intact; version/release commit and full project check remain owned by root.
